target_customer: Event hosts and businesses needing short notice licensed security guards
problem: Booking vetted security guards quickly was slow and opaque.
business_model: Marketplace matching customers with local guard companies, flat hourly rate

technical_complexity.rationale: Booking site and app with dispatch and payments; the hard part was vetting and supply of licensed guards.

defensibility.rationale: Supply relationships with guard companies and compliance checks, but little technical barrier.

market_need_then: TechCrunch June 2014 described demand for short notice guards at events, with Speakeasy and Zendesk named as customers and a flat 35 dollars per guard per hour.

branding.domain_note: Operates on bannerman.com; acquisition history not found.

brand_strength.rationale: TechCrunch, PYMNTS and Springwise covered it as an Uber for security guards, a clear pitch, but no mascot or community evidence.

pivots.from: On demand bouncers for events in San Francisco
pivots.to: Nationwide matching with local guard companies in all 50 states
pivots.why: Not stated; the company site says it is not a security company and the matched firm provides and bills the guards.

outcome_analysis: Bannerman launched on demand guard booking in San Francisco in 2014 and later broadened to a national matching service, with funding reported to 2018 by one database. YC lists it as inactive but the company site is still live with a 2026 copyright, so the outcome is a conflict and no failure story is established.
notes: CB Insights shows about 3.68M raised over four rounds; only the 3.56M undisclosed round dated 2018-03-09 and the YC and FundersClub seed era are recorded, so about 2 rounds are missing. Slow Ventures is a listed investor (F4 Fund) but not tied to a round. Status conflict: YC Inactive and Johnny Chin listed as former founder per third party, versus live site. Competitor: TechCrunch named none; later firms eGuards and RSPNDR postdate the batch. Founder backgrounds not found.
